sourcedFrom: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. (2024)
cleanIntro: A 9mm 1911-pattern pistol with a reverse recoil spring plug, a Shok-Buff on the guide rod, and a backstrap that swings away on the included takedown tool. Wilson Combat's maintenance schedule is round-counted: a quick clean every 300 rounds, a thorough clean and Shok-Buff check every 1,200, and the extractor and firing pin out every 6,000. ⛔ The thumb safety must be DOWN before the slide will move, and the slide is never slammed or dropped on an empty chamber — ease it down.

steps.title: Magazine out first, and set it aside
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger outside the trigger guard. Press the magazine release and take the magazine out of the grip before you touch the slide, then put it somewhere away from the pistol.
steps.prose: The order matters: working the slide with a magazine still seated feeds a fresh round into the chamber, and an empty pistol stops being empty.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and set it aside.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 2, p.39

steps.title: Thumb safety down, then retract the slide
steps.action: Push the thumb safety on the left rear of the frame down to FIRE. Then pull the slide fully back to extract and eject anything in the chamber, and lock it back on the slide stop.
steps.prose: With the safety up on SAFE the slide is blocked and will not move at all — that is the safety doing its job, not a jam. Do not force the slide against it.
steps.quote: The slide will not retract, and you will not be able to load the handgun if the safety is in the SAFE (up)(a) position.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Loading the Chamber and Activating the Safety, p.27

steps.title: Look and feel: chamber empty, magazine out
steps.action: With the slide locked back, look into the chamber and down the magazine well, then put a fingertip into the chamber. Both checks, every time — a cartridge that hides from the eye in a dark chamber cannot hide from a finger.
steps.prose: Wilson Combat asks for the check to be both visual and physical, and only then is the pistol unloaded.
steps.quote: Visually and physically confirm there is not a cartridge in the chamber, and the magazine is not in the handgun.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Unloading, step 3, p.30

steps.title: Eye protection on, takedown tool to hand
steps.action: Put on safety glasses before you start, and have the takedown tool that came with the pistol (or an equivalent) on the bench — the backstrap step needs it.
steps.prose: There are springs under compression in this strip, the recoil spring above all, and a spring that gets away goes for your face.
steps.quote: Wear adequate eye protection when disassembling this or any firearm.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 1, p.39

steps.title: Align the takedown notch, push the slide stop out
steps.action: Ease the slide forward from lock-back and draw it back just until the takedown notch in the slide lines up with the slide stop's lug. Then push the slide stop all the way out and take it off the frame.
steps.prose: Line the notch up first. Pushing a slide stop out against a misaligned slide is how the frame gets a scratched arc beside the pin hole.
steps.quote: Retract the slide to align the take down notch of the slide with the inner lug of the slide stop, completely push the slide stop out and remove.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 3, p.40

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame, fingers cupped over the spring
steps.action: Run the slide assembly forward off the front of the frame, with your fingers cupped under it so the recoil spring and guide cannot jump out as the slide clears.
steps.prose: The spring is still under tension when the slide comes off. Cupped fingers keep it, its guide and the Shok-Buff on the guide rod from launching across the room.
steps.quote: Slide the assembly forward to remove from the frame, while capturing the recoil spring and guide with your fingers cupped.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 4, p.41

steps.title: Ease the recoil spring, then spring, guide and plug out
steps.action: Let the recoil spring's tension off slowly under your fingers, then lift the spring and its guide rod out of the slide. Then take the recoil spring plug out of the slide.
steps.prose: Slowly is the instruction. The guide rod carries the Shok-Buff at its base, so keep the assembly together and note which way it sat.
steps.aside: 6. Remove the recoil spring plug from the slide.
steps.quote: Carefully ease the recoil spring to relax it’s tension, then remove the recoil spring and guide from the slide assembly.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 5, p.42

steps.title: Link forward and down, barrel out
steps.action: Swing the barrel link forward until it folds down against the underside of the chamber, then draw the barrel out of the slide.
steps.prose: With the link folded flat the barrel passes out of the slide freely. If it hangs up, the link has not folded all the way.
steps.quote: Pivot the barrel link forward and down against the underside of the barrel chamber and pull the barrel out of the slide.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 7, p.43

steps.title: Hammer down carefully onto its rest
steps.action: On the frame, lower the hammer under control so it rests against the front of the hammer slot. Do not let it fall freely.
steps.prose: ⛔ Wilson Combat warns that skipping this step can damage the pistol: the backstrap that comes off next holds the hammer spring housing, and it is released against the hammer at rest.
steps.quote: Lower the hammer carefully, so it is at rest with the front of the hammer slot in the frame. Failure to do so can damage your firearm.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 8, p.44
steps.warn: Failure to do so can damage your firearm.

steps.title: Takedown tool in, backstrap swings away
steps.action: Put the included takedown tool into the hole at the bottom of the frame and compress the hammer spring housing, while pressing upward on the bottom of the backstrap's beavertail. When the backstrap swings freely, pivot it away from the grips.
steps.prose: Both pressures at once — the tool compressing the housing and your thumb lifting the beavertail. With only one, the backstrap stays put.
steps.aside: The backstrap will swing freely. Now, pivot the backstrap away from the grips.
steps.quote: Insert the included takedown tool in the hole at the bottom of the frame, compress the hammer spring housing at the same time, while placing upward pressure on the bottom of the backstrap beavertail.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 9, p.45

steps.title: Grip panels off
steps.action: Unscrew the grip screws and lift the grip panels off the frame. Use a driver that fits the screws properly so you do not strip them or damage the threads.
steps.prose: Wilson Combat's grip section adds the care point: take the screws out carefully so neither the heads nor the threads are damaged.
steps.quote: Unscrew the grip panels and remove them off of the frame.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 10, p.46

steps.title: Field strip complete — inspect every part
steps.action: That is the strip as Wilson Combat writes it: slide, barrel, recoil spring and guide with the Shok-Buff, the recoil spring plug, the slide stop, the backstrap swung away and the grip panels off. Look every part over for abnormal wear or breakage now.
steps.prose: Any part showing damage, unusual wear or breakage means the pistol is not used until Wilson Combat has been contacted. The firing pin and the extractor are a round-count job, in Deep Clean.
steps.quote: You now have the frame disassembled as needed for normal cleaning and lubrication. Inspect all parts for abnormal wear and breakage at this time.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the PROJECT 1 Pistol, step 11, p.46

steps.title: The bore: slow, full-length strokes with a nylon brush
steps.action: Put a 9mm nylon bore brush on a cleaning rod, wet it with bore cleaner, and run it through the bore several times, pushing all the way through on every stroke. Let it stand 3 to 5 minutes, then run patches on a slotted tip until they come out clean.
steps.prose: Full-length strokes, not short scrubbing — reversing a brush halfway down the bore is hard on the brush and the rod.
steps.aside: Run the brush through the bore several times, pushing the rod all the way through.
steps.quote: When cleaning the bore, use slow complete strokes (full length of bore) with a properly sized nylon brush.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — For Reliable Function, Clean And Lubricate, p.47

steps.title: Muzzle and compensator area every 200–300 rounds
steps.action: Inspect and clean the muzzle and compensator area of the barrel to keep the carbon from building up. This one can be done with the pistol assembled: lock the slide open and work at the muzzle.
steps.prose: How often depends on how clean your ammunition burns; dirty ammunition means sooner.
steps.quote: Inspect and clean the muzzle and compensator area of the barrel to minimize carbon buildup and maintain optimal performance.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Maintenance schedule, Every 200-300 rounds, p.50

steps.title: Wipe away dirt and fouling, inside and out
steps.action: Wipe the slide and frame rails, the breech face, the barrel exterior and the chamber with non-abrasive patches or swabs. Where the inside of the pistol is caked with carbon, apply a carbon remover or bore cleaner first and let it work.
steps.prose: Non-abrasive is the word that matters on a finished pistol: nothing that scratches the rails or the finish.
steps.quote: Wipe away dirt and fouling on the interior and exterior of the firearm with non-abrasive patches or swabs.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — For Reliable Function, Clean And Lubricate, p.47

steps.title: Shok-Buff off the guide rod and inspected, every clean
steps.action: Take the Shok-Buff off the base of the guide rod, look at both sides, and replace it if it is cut, torn or swollen. Wipe the guide rod with a clean patch. Refit it with the groove at the top of the Shok-Buff aligned with the base of the guide rod, before the recoil spring goes back on.
steps.prose: ⚠ At the minimum the buffer is replaced every 1,200 rounds whatever it looks like. Wilson Combat recommends it for general use but the pistol runs safely without one.
steps.quote: At the minimum, replace the buffer every 1200 rounds.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Inspecting The Shok-Buff, p.54

steps.title: Light oil on the barrel locking surfaces and the rails
steps.action: After cleaning, put a light film of oil on the moving parts — the barrel locking surfaces and lugs, the barrel hood, and the frame and slide rails. Light, not heavy.
steps.prose: Wilson Combat's lubricant chart picks the oil by temperature: the regular oil at 60 degrees or warmer, the light oil below that. Do not over-lubricate; excess oil holds grit.
steps.quote: Make sure to lubricate the barrel locking surfaces and frame/slide rails.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — For Reliable Function, Clean And Lubricate, p.47

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Glasses on, rear of the slide pointed somewhere safe
deepSteps.action: Every 6,000 rounds, Wilson Combat has the firing pin out for cleaning and a new firing pin spring. Put on safety glasses and point the rear of the slide away from yourself and anyone else before you touch the firing pin stop.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The firing pin is under spring pressure and leaves the slide hard if you let it. Wilson Combat's own warning is that it will shoot out as in any 1911.
deepSteps.quote: Note: The firing pin will shoot out like in a 1911. Safety glasses need to be worn here.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.51
deepSteps.warn: Modern firearms contain springs that are under compression and can eject with significant striking force causing eye or other bodily injury.

deepSteps.title: Cover plate off (or work beneath the optic)
deepSteps.action: If your slide has the cover plate, unscrew both screws and slide the plate off the rear of the slide to expose the firing pin and its stop. If an optic is mounted instead, the firing pin stop works the same way and the same steps follow.
deepSteps.prose: The rear sight's set screws pass through the cover plate: Wilson Combat limits them to 15 in-lb on reassembly, because more bows the plate and moves your zero.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the cover plate by unscrewing both screws and carefully sliding it off the rear of the slide to expose the firing pin and firing pin stop.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.52

deepSteps.title: Punch the firing pin in, stop down and out
deepSteps.action: Hold the rear of the slide firmly and press the firing pin in with a 1/8-inch punch to take the spring pressure off the stop. Keep a finger on the firing pin while you slide the stop down and out of the way, so the pin cannot eject.
deepSteps.prose: Your finger on the pin is what keeps it in the slide. Take it away before the stop is clear and the pin goes.
deepSteps.quote: Use your finger to retain the firing pin while sliding the stop down and out of the way.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.52

deepSteps.title: Let the spring out slowly, then spring off the pin
deepSteps.action: Let the firing pin spring release its compression slowly, then take the pin and spring out of the slide. Separate them by turning the firing pin clockwise while pulling the spring firmly off. Clean the firing pin channel, and fit a new firing pin spring when it goes back in — the old one is discarded.
deepSteps.prose: The firing pin spring is part of the drop safety: Wilson Combat has it replaced every 5,000 rounds of live fire or 5,000 dry fires.
deepSteps.aside: Slowly allow the firing pin spring to release its compressed spring tension and then remove it from the slide.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin spring from the firing pin by turning the firing pin clockwise and firmly pulling off the spring.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.52

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin: heat first, then out with the hex wrench
deepSteps.action: With the cover plate or optic off, the extractor is held by a threaded pin set in threadlocker. Heat the bottom of the extractor pin area of the slide with a torch or soldering iron to break the bond, then turn the pin counterclockwise with the supplied .050 hex wrench, holding the extractor with your hand as the pin comes out.
deepSteps.prose: Heat is needed the first time because of the threadlocker. Keep a hand on the extractor — it is sprung and leaves its pocket when the pin clears.
deepSteps.quote: Retain the extractor with your hand while removing the pin.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Extractor Removal/Cleaning, p.56

deepSteps.title: Extractor and pocket clean, dry underneath
deepSteps.action: Clean the carbon off the extractor and out of the extractor pocket thoroughly. Replace the extractor spring now. Leave no excess oil under the extractor when it goes back, then reassemble in reverse order and test it with a dummy round under the hook.
deepSteps.prose: Oil pooled under the extractor collects carbon and stops it closing on the case rim — exactly the failure to extract this job is meant to cure.
deepSteps.aside: Test your extractor by placing a dummy round under your extractor hook.
deepSteps.quote: Do not leave excessive oil or lubricant under the extractor pocket when reassembling.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for DIVISION 77 – PROJECT 1 Handgun — Copyright© 2024 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Extractor Removal/Cleaning, p.56

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: 9mm nylon brush with bore cleaner, full-length strokes from end to end
Stand 3 to 5 minutes, then patches until clean
Muzzle and compensator area cleaned every 200-300 rounds

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and the inside of the slide wiped with non-abrasive patches
Carbon remover on anything caked, then wiped

cleaning.name: SHOK-BUFF
tasks: Off the guide rod, both sides inspected
Replaced if cut, torn or swollen — and every 1,200 rounds regardless
Refitted with its groove aligned to the base of the guide rod

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Light oil on the barrel locking surfaces, lugs and hood
Light oil on the frame and slide rails

reassembly: Grip panels back on the frame and their screws tightened carefully.
Backstrap pivoted back into place against the grip.
Barrel back into the slide with the link folded forward and down; recoil spring plug back in.
Shok-Buff on the base of the guide rod with its groove aligned, then the recoil spring and guide back into the slide assembly.
Slide assembly back onto the frame from the front, the takedown notch aligned with the slide stop, and the slide stop pushed back in.
Wilson Combat's instruction is to reverse the field strip steps; ease the slide forward on the empty pistol — never let it slam.
fncheck: Unloaded and proven, magazine out, muzzle in a safe direction — Wilson Combat asks for this test after every disassembly and reassembly. Thumb safety: cock the hammer, push the safety up to SAFE and press the trigger — the safety stays on and the hammer does not move. Disconnector: with the hammer cocked, draw the slide back ¼ to ½ inch and press the trigger — the hammer must not fall. Half-cock: set the hammer on half-cock and press the trigger with a full grip — the hammer must not move. If the hammer falls or moves in any of these, or you see it follow to half-cock when the slide closes, do not use the pistol and contact Wilson Combat.
